answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making new identities costly to scale. Before a newcomer can spend or attest, two established peers must lock a copper deposit against its name for a full epoch. That bond begins a spiral of shared liability: later unique-work checks either strengthen the identity or, if it is exposed as a clone, slash the sponsors and freeze the fake. After a clean window, sponsors reclaim the stake and the proven agent may transplant its reputation as freely as a willow cutting, so honest participants keep mobility while mass-produced replicas remain unprofitable.
